doc.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020

title: What he does when he sits down at a session
summary: Bergeron on whether the music is on the stand, glancing ahead, and warming up.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: So when you get to a date and you get there early, is the music on the stand, and what is the first thing that you look for?

The music sometimes is on the stand at that point but maybe not, maybe they’re just passing it out. Warren Luening used to say — he never looked at the music. And he’d go, “Oh don’t look at it, it’s going to scare you.” You know, and so he’d just leave the book closed and we’d open it up — and that’s kind of what I usually do anyway. You know I look ahead a little bit sometimes, depending on who the writer is, you know, because I know this person has a tendency to write a little more difficult than some of the other © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

composers so I might just thumb through, what have we got here. Oh let me take a look at this real quick. You know. So I’ll just finger through it or maybe put my mute in and play a hard lick or something. But most of the stuff is kind of another day in the office for the most part. You come in and just read it down and it’s not so difficult that it can’t be read down. But there are things that can be very, very challenging. So I glance at the music a little bit and then I just carry on with my warm-up.
